nodes.title: Shared git-data

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). BORN (ADR-149); the store is EMPTY until the LUKS cutover (#5274) flips `GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` (every write path is gated on that flag, #6976). The host reports its own boot correctness off-host (#6982, ADR-149 item 1): boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal, and gc faults to Better Stack. The birth route is gated MECHANICALLY by `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate`, which refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template (a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload) and, since #8010, names a completed, successful `workflow_dispatch` run of the rehearsal workflow on `main` that uploaded a boot-evidence artifact and whose `head_sha` re-hashes to that evidence (resolved live through the GitHub REST API), with the Sentry cross-check verdict required in the file. CI root access for the cutover is ADR-220's (see the github -> gitDataStore edge). AT REST: from PR1 of #8211 (ADR-239) the render ALWAYS serves the LUKS mapper `/dev/mapper/git-data` (`hcloud_volume.git_data_luks`, git-data-luks.tf) at `/mnt/git-data`, from boot — there is no plaintext/LUKS selector and no runtime repoint, and the serving change reached production through an ordinary `git_data_host_replace` (ADR-237 post-merge step 3) while the store was empty and `GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` was off. The first such replace (2026-09-24) destroyed the last host that served the PLAINTEXT ext4 `hcloud_volume.git_data` (`format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) and FATALed on that volume's dirty journal; the replace carrying the forward fix (ADR-239 amendment 2026-09-24) booted a host on 2026-09-25 (run 36118115758) that serves the still-empty store from the LUKS mapper (ADR-239 accepted 2026-09-27). That plaintext volume is RETAINED and is never mounted: once per instance it is set kernel read-only and read through a throwaway dm snapshot whose copy-on-write lives in RAM (ADR-239 amendment 2026-09-24), only to prove its post-journal-replay tree holds no repository; it stays a ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897) until the post-soak wipe. Every store-acting script refuses unless `findmnt -n -o SOURCE --mountpoint /mnt/git-data` EQUALS the mapper and the bootstrap has written /etc/git-data/store-verified. Since #8210 the LUKS mapper is reopened on EVERY boot by a systemd oneshot that fetches the passphrase from Doppler at boot (never from disk), so the store survives a reboot rather than silently vanishing at the first one

description.txt: DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.

OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Booted (since #8714 step 5.3b-iii, 2026-09-28) from the pinned GitHub release asset that mirrors the upstream image byte-for-byte, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement), and never from ghcr.io, which the host name-resolution-denies (see the zotRegistry -> github edge). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-09-20 (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The preceding CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING clause, which asserted the live device was unencrypted pending an unfired `registry-luks-recut` (#6929), is RETRACTED 2026-09-20 (#8386) — and it was already spent when written, since the recut fired 2026-08-10, as the pinned-image clause above this one records. What settled it is an off-host measurement rather than a job log: since #8386 the SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK heartbeat carries store_mount_src / store_backing_dev / store_mount_devid / store_expected_devid / store_luks in its trusted region, and boot b3ec6c3b (delivered by registry-host-replace run 35489418603) reads store_luks=yes with store_mount_devid == store_expected_devid == scsi-0HC_Volume_106585109 across 120 rows. encryption-posture-ledger.json's `hcloud_volume.registry` row therefore reads live_verification: available. Read the heartbeat, not this description, whenever the two could diverge. Scope: that measurement says the store SITS ON a LUKS container, not that the passphrase still opens it (the escrow re-test and the standing alert are #8408), and the reboot window in which zot could serve a root-fs directory is measured and graded (the registry_store_not_luks alert). Since #8408 zot start is gated on the LUKS filesystem's sentinel on EVERY container start (a --mount bind of /var/lib/zot/.soleur-luks-sentinel; the NIC guard starts it within one tick once the store returns), and the passphrase is re-tested daily (store_escrow= on SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK) — both delivered on boot 5639cc07 (registry-host-replace run 35672138112, 2026-09-22; PR #8456); read the heartbeat for the live answer. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.

Keyless container-image signing/verification (cosign/Fulcio/Rekor). The release CI keyless-signs the pushed web app image digest (this IS a live sigstore call — github → sigstore below). The host then cosign-verifies the signature FULLY OFFLINE against a pinned trusted_root.json — it makes NO live sigstore call at verify time (ADR-087, #6005) — supply-chain authenticity for the shared host (#5933 Item 4).

description.txt: Inngest durable queue + run-state. AOF on the persistent volume survives a host re-provision — the armed-reminder durability fix (#5450). AT REST: LUKS-ENCRYPTED since the additive cutover of 2026-09-20 (#8296). The live store is hcloud_volume.inngest_redis_luks, opened as mapper inngest-redis and mounted at /mnt/data; the passphrase is minted at merge and held in Doppler (inngest-redis-luks.tf), and inngest-luks-open.service reopens the mapper on every boot. The encryption-posture ledger records that row as mechanism luks. RETAINED PLAINTEXT BACKSTOP: the pre-cutover volume hcloud_volume.inngest_redis stays attached and intact, holding a full plaintext copy of the AOF as of the cutover freeze, so that op=luks-rollback on cutover-inngest.yml (ADR-225) is a mount move plus a reverse copy; it is retired under #8285 (expires 2026-10-22) and until then a seized or snapshot-imaged backstop exposes in-flight job payloads. A probe row reporting /mnt/data on anything other than the encrypted volume pages via logtail_exploration_alert.inngest_luks_wrong_volume, and scripts/followthroughs/inngest-luks-property-8296.sh, once enrolled on #8285, cross-checks the ledger claim against the device daily. A probe pipeline that goes silent reads as healthy to the alert, so #8516 added the dead-man's-switch sibling betteruptime_heartbeat.inngest_server_probe (uptime-alerts.tf — born paused; its feeder + arming are tracked on #9703). The authority for which volume holds the store is the durable pointer INNGEST_LUKS_ACTIVE_VOLUME_ID, not a signature on a device (ADR-142).

PRIVATE GHCR registry (ghcr.io/jikig-ai/soleur-web-platform + soleur-inngest-bootstrap) — the ORIGINAL host pull source, now WRITE-ONLY: still dual-pushed by CI, but DEAD AS A FALLBACK since the Phase-5 retirement — the read PAT is revoked (GET api.github.com/user -> 401) and the minter was disabled (GHCR_MINTER_DISABLED=true; pull-token mint -> 403 DENIED), verified 2026-07-30 (#7071); the minter, the PAT variables and their Doppler keys were deleted by ADR-096 task 5.4 (#8714). It receives every image and can serve none of its PRIVATE packages TO HOSTS (the host pull of the PUBLIC cosign verifier image was a separate edge until #8714 moved it to gcr.io — `hetzner -> sigstore`). Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. SINCE #8036 1c (2026-09-23) THE DEPLOY-PATH HOST-SIDE CODE IS DELETED, not merely dead, AND SINCE #8036 1d (2026-09-24, ADR-096 5.3b-i) THE FRESH-BOOT CODE TOO: no host presents a GHCR credential at boot — the web and inngest templates and the baked bootstrap script carry no GHCR login and no GHCR pull, and no templatefile() passes the GHCR credential into user_data (true of the templates at merge; of each host once it is replaced from them). The inngest templates keep the ghcr.io/…soleur-inngest-bootstrap tag@sha256 literal only as the bump bot's pin carrier; it is never pulled. ci-deploy.sh has no `docker login ghcr.io`, no auth-recovery re-fetch and no fallback branch, and it sweeps the revoked inline credential out of the deploy docker config on every deploy. So “dead edge” is now a statement about code that no longer exists rather than about a credential that cannot authenticate. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).

The PUBLIC upstream release surface (github.com/inngest/inngest) that publishes the self-hosted `inngest` binary — release tags, per-arch tarballs (inngest_<ver>_linux_{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz), and one release-shipped checksums.txt per version. Reached by two consumers with different trust semantics: the dedicated host's bootstrap downloads the version the committed `inngest_cli_version` pin names and sha256-verifies the tarball against the committed per-arch checksum before executing it (the reviewed embed in inngest.tf is the trust anchor, not the checksums file — it is a plain sha256sum manifest, not GPG-signed), and CI reaches it twice (build-inngest-bootstrap-image.yml downloads the same pinned tarball for the bootstrap image; the `Detect inngest CLI pin drift` poll in rule-audit.yml reads the releases listing to measure the pinned-version delta, #7463). Added 2026-09-29 (#7463) because the edge was unmodeled while the pin sat 29 stable releases behind with no freshness owner — the gap #7308 named. FRESHNESS OWNER (mirrors the projectZot/node discipline): no bot mutates the pin; detection is the rule-audit.yml poll (1st + 15th — files one idempotent `inngest-pin-drift` issue); enforcement is apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-cli-staleness.test.sh in deploy-script-tests; the analysis of record is apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-cli.provenance.md; the sub-second liveness probe is inngest-cli-pin-probe.sh.

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2. ALSO (#8122, ADR-219): the UPSTREAM CONTENT SOURCE for every schema-conforming vendored bundle — goSprinto/compliance-skills (gdpr-gate rules) and General-Legal/legal-templates (legal-generate corpus, added here as the second upstream) — polled by cron-content-vendor-drift via the git/trees + git/blobs API against per-bundle NOTICE pins.

DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.

@playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha), spawned by npx as a stdio JSON-RPC child — one newline-terminated JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (measured) — driving a HEADED real Chrome (channel chrome, chromiumSandbox true, X11 forced at the env level) on the operator workstation with the persistent profile ~/.cache/playwright-mcp-profile (this repository's registration claims it, or a numbered sibling directory when it is held, by a kernel flock tied to the proxy process — slot 0 may wait up to 7 s, for the same session's previous launch or an unknown/unreadable owner — so a new-style launch or /mcp reconnect kills nothing; an old-style launch string still running in another worktree can, and the plugin registration has no lease), whose password manager autofills into pages the agent opens. An accessibility snapshot serialises the VALUE of every input, so a bare browser_snapshot on a login page or a credential panel returns the value inline in the tool result. Since #7980 the agent runtime reaches this server THROUGH the plugin's snapshotGuard component rather than directly — that relay is the trust boundary this node exists to show — and only on a registration that routes through it: this repository's .mcp.json does, and since #8156 the plugin's own plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registration does by default (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*, on the dedicated soleur-playwright-mcp-profile under the XDG cache root — that registration ships NO config and no display forcing, so it runs the upstream defaults: headed, channel chrome; on a host with no Google Chrome executable its opt-in --chromium-fallback proxy flag makes the proxy append --browser chromium --sandbox, so Playwright launches its bundled Chromium instead with the Chromium sandbox kept on (a host that cannot run it fails closed: install Google Chrome), and its env carries only PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS=0, an inert guard on stdio, not the fix for anything — ADR-271); a customer's own registration does not unless they route it themselves; the hosted agent-runner registers no Playwright server (the vendored plugin tree excludes the plugin-root .mcp.json — both vendor steps rm it post-copy, so the hosted plugins:[type local] load never discovers it); the Inngest fleet's per-fire cron-ux-audit overlay runs a SEPARATE 0.0.75 copy, UNWRAPPED, with --snapshot-mode none appended directly (register PA-31 §(g)). Every behaviour cited is a dated observation of the pinned version, not an undertaking about the tool; the suite derives its fixture directory from the pin, so a bump without a re-capture reddens.

Used to confirm the DNS-only flip actually reached the public internet before the cert poll begins — Cloudflare's TTL for proxied records is fixed at 300 s, so a proxy-status flip takes ~5-10 min to propagate and a poll started before then is guaranteed-wasted public-TLS-outage window. `dig` is deliberately NOT used: it is not installed in the app image (the Dockerfile installs only ca-certificates, git, bubblewrap, socat, qpdf, jq), so shelling out would throw at runtime.

plugins/soleur/ — skills, agents, knowledge base, AND the shared bash primitives shipped for execution on an installed user's machine (ADR-178, #7409): scripts/lib/session-state.sh is the cross-session lock/lease layer that gates worktree reaping AND, since #8400, branch deletion: `cleanup-merged` keys its lease check on the BRANCH rather than on a worktree path, so a merged branch whose worktree was already removed is now held by a live lease instead of reaching `git push origin --delete` and `git branch -D`. The narrower wording was falsified by that change, in the same way and at the same time as the script's own fail-closed banner. It lived under .claude/hooks/ until #7409, i.e. outside the subtree marketplace.json copies, so every installed user ran with that layer silently replaced by no-op stubs. What this system SHIPS is therefore not only prose for an agent to read — it includes executable concurrency primitives whose absence is unobservable to the user. Since ADR-254 (#8880) it also ships a user-machine WRITE surface: `scripts/emit-decision.sh` appends field-allowlisted decision records to the project-local `.soleur/decisions.jsonl` (NO-ECHO metadata only, `.soleur/.gitignore` self-guard, ~5 MB rotation, tester-owned, no egress — the aggregate reaches Jikigai only when a tester runs `alpha-metrics.sh` and pastes it at checkpoint). Since ADR-264 it also ships the staged, agent-runnable operator-script contract (`scripts/lib/operator-script.sh`: --list, --stage, --stage --apply --plan-digest, exit 75) and the PreToolUse hook `hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh` registered in `hooks/hooks.json`, which reaches a founder's install and is loaded by web Concierge too (the web runtime opts it out until the web approval adapter lands). A further write surface lands with #9403 (ADR-268): `scripts/pipeline-tally.sh` mutates per-branch work-unit counters under `<git-common>/soleur-session-state/counters/` (key=value, flock-serialized, units only — never dollars) and `hooks/stop-hook.sh` READS the ledger's `capped` key as a hard-cap floor; the ledger is repo-local machine state with no egress, and ship renders its counts into the public PR body as a `## Pipeline Tally` section. Since ADR-250 Amendment 2 (#9677) `cleanup-merged` can also, on explicit opt-in, delete expired entries from the plugin's own scratch-quarantine directory under /tmp and /var/tmp (`SOLEUR_QUARANTINE_DRAIN=1`, a terminal delete on the user's machine scoped to that directory) and prune old Docker build cache and dangling images (`SOLEUR_DOCKER_PRUNE`, dry-run first, never volumes or containers); both print stdout markers (on a user's machine they stay there; the web platform's telemetry mirror forwards them like every other SOLEUR_* marker).

nodes.title: Hook Engine

description.txt: Guards tool calls (blocks commits to main, rm -rf, etc.) AND injects additive context — phase-surface hints (ADR-070) and declarative skill context_queries (ADR-086). CONSUMES a MODEL-CONTROLLED tool-call envelope on stdin: that input is untrusted and is parsed without shell evaluation, with each contracted field type-asserted rather than coerced (ADR-156, #7164 — an array tool_input.command previously reached eval AND evaded every anchored guard). Prior description said only what hooks DO, never what they CONSUME. A PreToolUse hook also has a THIRD disposition beyond allow/deny: it may REWRITE tool_input before execution and let the call proceed (ADR-162, #7165) — grep-rewrite.sh prepends a grep() redefinition that neutralizes the ugrep shim which reached 9.5 GB RSS against a 21 kB file, leaving the command byte-identical. Bounded by a SINGLE-REWRITER invariant: updatedInput REPLACES tool_input (it does not merge), a sibling deny still wins, and permission rules match the ORIGINAL command. Since ADR-264 there are exactly TWO named rewriters: the shipped plugin hook `plugins/soleur/hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh` turns the harness approval prompt into the human acknowledgement of a generated operator script's production write — it recognises the script by its `SOLEUR-GENERATED-OPERATOR-SCRIPT v2` header content, mints a one-time command-bound receipt (a record named sha256(nonce) under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/soleur/approvals`, 0700/0600, 10-minute expiry, local state with no persistent store), rewrites the command to carry the nonce, and answers ask (interactive), defer then a resume marker (headless), or deny (bypass modes, unknown mode); it FAILS CLOSED for a candidate command and never for a non-candidate, and the web runtime opts it out via SOLEUR_DISABLE_OPERATOR_STAGE_APPROVAL_HOOK=1 from buildAgentEnv (ADR-162 amendment 2026-10-01). The receipt is a same-user file: it resists an instruction-following agent, not a hijacked one. Additionally, in the repo-local `.claude/` hook surface only — never the shipped plugin surface — it enforces host resource control: at SessionStart it adopts the agent process tree into a memory-capped systemd transient scope (ADR-161). Since ADR-261 (#9239) that backstop's DISPATCH is version-independent: settings.json execs a stable resolver shim (memory-backstop-resolve.sh) that selects the highest-BACKSTOP_REVISION copy across the checkout, the managed path ~/.local/share/soleur/hooks/, and the two plugin caches; a strictly-newer winner self-publishes to the managed path (flock-serialized) BEFORE exec, the schema:2 ledger records resolved_from/backstop_revision/repaired, and repair_stale_scopes runtime-converges stale-adopted scope caps at any SessionStart (ADR-159 applied to transient scopes). The resolver itself cannot self-upgrade — a stale checkout keeps its stale shim — but sweep-repair still reaches the scopes a stale shim's hook created. That surface split is scoped to resource control and must not be read as a general one: since ADR-227 (#8323) the SHIPPED plugin surface is itself a compaction-lifecycle consumer AND, for the first time, STATEFUL ACROSS EVENTS: `hooks/compaction-state.sh` writes a per-session ledger under `${TMPDIR}/soleur-compaction/` at `PreCompact` and reads it at `SessionStart:compact`. Every other hook here is a stateless single-event transformer, so this is a new property of the container rather than a new instance of an existing one. The ledger is machine-local, session-keyed, mode 0700, reaped at 7 days, and deliberately outside the user git tree — `hooks/compaction-state.sh` binds `PreCompact` and `SessionStart:compact`, so a customer install now carries hook code that runs on events the repo-local surface never handled. Because a plugin hook is global, that consumer is gated on a two-conjunct scope guard (a `plugins/soleur` directory AND a Soleur plan/spec artifact) rather than on `is-inside-work-tree`, which is true in every customer repo. Where this container runs server-side there is no per-user systemd bus, so that path declines and does nothing. HARNESS SURFACES: `.claude/hooks/` (Claude Code) is the only tree of hook CODE since 2026-09-23 (ADR-245, #8306), which retired the hand-ported PreToolUse mirrors; ADR-165's split-by-reason-class posture described those mirrors and is historical. One hook PREDICATE does have a second implementation outside this tree: the filing gate's `lib/filing-shape.pl` classifier is mirrored by `filingShape()` in the cron containment hook (apps/web-platform/server/inngest/cron-bash-allowlist-hook.mjs), and the two are bound only by the shared corpus `lib/filing-shape-corpus.json`, which both suites run (ADR-256, #9089). Dispatch REGISTRIES are per-harness and audited (#8205, ADR-223): `.claude/settings.json` is Claude-canonical (its lowercase `^write$`/`^ask_user_question$` twins serve Grok and coincidentally cover those tools under Devin), `.devin/config.json` binds the triaged hook set on anchored Devin wire names (Claude matchers there are loaded-but-dead), `.codex/config.toml` serves its harness, and `.claude/hooks/devin-dispositions.tsv` + `devin-matcher-parity.test.sh` keep the audit honest. On the `.claude` side exit 0 is the precondition for that posture at all: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout JSON entirely (#7190). That single-tree statement describes where hook CODE lives; since ADR-178 (#7409) it no longer describes where its concurrency layer comes from — `lib/incidents.sh`, `lib/log-rotation.sh` and `pre-merge-rebase.sh` source the session-state lock/lease primitives from a THIRD, shipped location inside the deployed plugin root, reaching in from the repo side. Its TELEMETRY has a namespace contract (ADR-205, #7853): an emitted rule_id carrying a section prefix (hr/wg/cq/rf/pdr/cm) CLAIMS membership in the AGENTS corpus and is orphan-checked against it; one carrying no prefix is hook telemetry and is outside the corpus by construction, which replaced nine hand-maintained exemption stanzas in rule-metrics-aggregate.sh. Under test the sink is redirected at the RUNNER CHOKEPOINT — both bunfig preloads, the vitest globalSetup, the test-helpers.sh prelude and the _git_fixture_env import — never at the call site, and never by teaching this container to detect tests, because a false positive there would darken real operator telemetry.

description.txt: The operator's own per-user systemd manager, reached over the D-Bus socket at /run/user/<uid>/bus (SO_PEERCRED-authenticated, same uid only, no network). Owns the cgroup v2 hierarchy for the login session: the Hook Engine asks IT to create the memory-capped transient scope each agent session runs in, so systemd stays the SINGLE WRITER to that hierarchy and no component writes cgroup directories directly (ADR-161). Units are transient and self-clean when their last process exits, so nothing is provisioned and nothing persists across a reboot.

plugins/soleur/ — skills, agents, knowledge base, AND the shared bash primitives shipped for execution on an installed user's machine (ADR-178, #7409): scripts/lib/session-state.sh is the cross-session lock/lease layer that gates worktree reaping AND, since #8400, branch deletion: `cleanup-merged` keys its lease check on the BRANCH rather than on a worktree path, so a merged branch whose worktree was already removed is now held by a live lease instead of reaching `git push origin --delete` and `git branch -D`. The narrower wording was falsified by that change, in the same way and at the same time as the script's own fail-closed banner. It lived under .claude/hooks/ until #7409, i.e. outside the subtree marketplace.json copies, so every installed user ran with that layer silently replaced by no-op stubs. What this system SHIPS is therefore not only prose for an agent to read — it includes executable concurrency primitives whose absence is unobservable to the user. Since ADR-254 (#8880) it also ships a user-machine WRITE surface: `scripts/emit-decision.sh` appends field-allowlisted decision records to the project-local `.soleur/decisions.jsonl` (NO-ECHO metadata only, `.soleur/.gitignore` self-guard, ~5 MB rotation, tester-owned, no egress — the aggregate reaches Jikigai only when a tester runs `alpha-metrics.sh` and pastes it at checkpoint). Since ADR-264 it also ships the staged, agent-runnable operator-script contract (`scripts/lib/operator-script.sh`: --list, --stage, --stage --apply --plan-digest, exit 75) and the PreToolUse hook `hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh` registered in `hooks/hooks.json`, which reaches a founder's install and is loaded by web Concierge too (the web runtime opts it out until the web approval adapter lands). A further write surface lands with #9403 (ADR-268): `scripts/pipeline-tally.sh` mutates per-branch work-unit counters under `<git-common>/soleur-session-state/counters/` (key=value, flock-serialized, units only — never dollars) and `hooks/stop-hook.sh` READS the ledger's `capped` key as a hard-cap floor; the ledger is repo-local machine state with no egress, and ship renders its counts into the public PR body as a `## Pipeline Tally` section. Since ADR-250 Amendment 2 (#9677) `cleanup-merged` can also, on explicit opt-in, delete expired entries from the plugin's own scratch-quarantine directory under /tmp and /var/tmp (`SOLEUR_QUARANTINE_DRAIN=1`, a terminal delete on the user's machine scoped to that directory) and prune old Docker build cache and dangling images (`SOLEUR_DOCKER_PRUNE`, dry-run first, never volumes or containers); both print stdout markers (on a user's machine they stay there; the web platform's telemetry mirror forwards them like every other SOLEUR_* marker).

nodes.title: browser-snapshot credential guard

description.txt: Four controls with one predicate (ADR-213 + its 2026-09-14 addendum, #7947/#7980): (1) redact-a11y-snapshot.py rewrites credential-NAMED input values in an accessibility tree to <redacted> — name-based, because no surface serialises type=; (2) browser-snapshot-credential-guard.sh, a PreToolUse DENY on any Bash-invoked agent-browser snapshot not piped through that redactor; (3) the corpus lint's S2 rule, which now prescribes a STRUCTURAL disclosure verbatim (use the filename: + redactor + shred form first; a refusal whose text starts `refused by playwright-mcp-redact-proxy:` means THAT server's registration is wrapped — any other error, such as the server's own File access denied, does not); (4) playwright-mcp-redact-proxy.py, a single-file stdio JSON-RPC relay that importlib-loads the redactor by path, runs redact_text over the text of EVERY tools/call result by shape (two tools inline tree lines on the pinned server — browser_snapshot and browser_find), appends --snapshot-mode none to the wrapped argv so action tools write no raw page-*.yml (and, only when started with the opt-in --chromium-fallback flag on a host with no Google Chrome executable, also appends --browser chromium --sandbox — not a sink flag; --no-sandbox, PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SANDBOX and config chromiumSandbox:false and --executable-path stay refused), refuses browser_snapshot with filename and any call carrying an undocumented _meta argument (measured: _meta.json returns the tree as one escaped string the line-anchored predicate cannot see), withholds a JSON-escaped tree in any result and an error carrying data or tree-shaped text, drops server notifications and every server request but roots/list, refuses to start on any launch setting that opens a raw sink around it (--save-session, a non-JSON or saveSession/saveVideo/server/non-vision-capabilities config, --port/--host, --caps beyond vision, --output-mode file, any DEBUG value that can enable a pw: logger, DEBUG_FILE), and is fail-closed in three arms with NO kill switch (cannot load or self-test the redactor → exit 2 before spawning; cannot rewrite a result → isError text that never quotes input; dead child → non-zero exit, closed stdin → group SIGTERM then SIGKILL, signalled to the GROUP even when the direct child has already exited). SHIPS vs WIRES: the plugin SHIPS the proxy and, since #8156, WIRES it — plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registers `playwright` through it (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*), alongside this repository's own .mcp.json; a customer's own registration stays wrapped only by their configuration. Residuals stay named, not closed: screenshots render a readonly credential panel in clear; browser_network_request / browser_evaluate / browser_run_code_unsafe return what they are asked for; console logs, PNGs and downloads are non-tree disk sinks; Page URL / title / dialog prose is inert to the predicate.

description.txt: @playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha), spawned by npx as a stdio JSON-RPC child — one newline-terminated JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (measured) — driving a HEADED real Chrome (channel chrome, chromiumSandbox true, X11 forced at the env level) on the operator workstation with the persistent profile ~/.cache/playwright-mcp-profile (this repository's registration claims it, or a numbered sibling directory when it is held, by a kernel flock tied to the proxy process — slot 0 may wait up to 7 s, for the same session's previous launch or an unknown/unreadable owner — so a new-style launch or /mcp reconnect kills nothing; an old-style launch string still running in another worktree can, and the plugin registration has no lease), whose password manager autofills into pages the agent opens. An accessibility snapshot serialises the VALUE of every input, so a bare browser_snapshot on a login page or a credential panel returns the value inline in the tool result. Since #7980 the agent runtime reaches this server THROUGH the plugin's snapshotGuard component rather than directly — that relay is the trust boundary this node exists to show — and only on a registration that routes through it: this repository's .mcp.json does, and since #8156 the plugin's own plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registration does by default (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*, on the dedicated soleur-playwright-mcp-profile under the XDG cache root — that registration ships NO config and no display forcing, so it runs the upstream defaults: headed, channel chrome; on a host with no Google Chrome executable its opt-in --chromium-fallback proxy flag makes the proxy append --browser chromium --sandbox, so Playwright launches its bundled Chromium instead with the Chromium sandbox kept on (a host that cannot run it fails closed: install Google Chrome), and its env carries only PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS=0, an inert guard on stdio, not the fix for anything — ADR-271); a customer's own registration does not unless they route it themselves; the hosted agent-runner registers no Playwright server (the vendored plugin tree excludes the plugin-root .mcp.json — both vendor steps rm it post-copy, so the hosted plugins:[type local] load never discovers it); the Inngest fleet's per-fire cron-ux-audit overlay runs a SEPARATE 0.0.75 copy, UNWRAPPED, with --snapshot-mode none appended directly (register PA-31 §(g)). Every behaviour cited is a dated observation of the pinned version, not an undertaking about the tool; the suite derives its fixture directory from the pin, so a bump without a re-capture reddens.

description.txt: Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2. ALSO (#8122, ADR-219): the UPSTREAM CONTENT SOURCE for every schema-conforming vendored bundle — goSprinto/compliance-skills (gdpr-gate rules) and General-Legal/legal-templates (legal-generate corpus, added here as the second upstream) — polled by cron-content-vendor-drift via the git/trees + git/blobs API against per-bundle NOTICE pins.

NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. var.web_hosts now has two keys: web-2 was provisioned 2026-07-27 (#6969) and is a scheduler-less cattle standby (web_colocate_inngest=false — no inngest-server.service, no local reminders). web-2's own /workspaces volume is a different story from web-1's: web-1 keeps the additive LUKS singleton (hcloud_volume.workspaces_luks, ADR-119) delivered by its Terraform SSH installer, while a fresh host takes the baked guest-side LUKS path (ADR-263) - one mechanism, two Terraform addresses - and until web-2's live conversion has run it is still plaintext-but-empty, gate-blocked from serving weight and from holding user data

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; that web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463). var.web_hosts has two keys again: a fresh cattle web-2 (10.0.1.11, #6969) was born 2026-07-27 after the gate merged, so it runs no connector; it is a scheduler-less standby (runs the #8495 watchdog dispatch clock), web_colocate_inngest=false.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (web-server-dispatched every 15 min, #8495; GHA cron fallback) (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

description.txt: OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Booted (since #8714 step 5.3b-iii, 2026-09-28) from the pinned GitHub release asset that mirrors the upstream image byte-for-byte, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement), and never from ghcr.io, which the host name-resolution-denies (see the zotRegistry -> github edge). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-09-20 (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The preceding CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING clause, which asserted the live device was unencrypted pending an unfired `registry-luks-recut` (#6929), is RETRACTED 2026-09-20 (#8386) — and it was already spent when written, since the recut fired 2026-08-10, as the pinned-image clause above this one records. What settled it is an off-host measurement rather than a job log: since #8386 the SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK heartbeat carries store_mount_src / store_backing_dev / store_mount_devid / store_expected_devid / store_luks in its trusted region, and boot b3ec6c3b (delivered by registry-host-replace run 35489418603) reads store_luks=yes with store_mount_devid == store_expected_devid == scsi-0HC_Volume_106585109 across 120 rows. encryption-posture-ledger.json's `hcloud_volume.registry` row therefore reads live_verification: available. Read the heartbeat, not this description, whenever the two could diverge. Scope: that measurement says the store SITS ON a LUKS container, not that the passphrase still opens it (the escrow re-test and the standing alert are #8408), and the reboot window in which zot could serve a root-fs directory is measured and graded (the registry_store_not_luks alert). Since #8408 zot start is gated on the LUKS filesystem's sentinel on EVERY container start (a --mount bind of /var/lib/zot/.soleur-luks-sentinel; the NIC guard starts it within one tick once the store returns), and the passphrase is re-tested daily (store_escrow= on SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK) — both delivered on boot 5639cc07 (registry-host-replace run 35672138112, 2026-09-22; PR #8456); read the heartbeat for the live answer. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.
